author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory page listing each specialty with its veterinarians
summary: A read-only page at /specialties.html lists every specialty by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name (first then last), all on one page with no paging.
acceptance_criteria: Given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then every specialty is shown by its stored name with the veterinarians holding it, all on a single page with no paging
Given a veterinarian holding a specialty, when the directory is opened, then that veterinarian is named in full, first name followed by last name (for example Helen Leary)
Given a specialty held by more than one veterinarian, when the directory is opened, then every holder is listed under that specialty
Given a specialty that no veterinarian holds, when the directory is opened, then that specialty still appears with no veterinarian listed under it
Given a veterinarian who holds no specialty, when the directory is opened, then that veterinarian is not shown anywhere on the page
Given the clinic's specialties, when the directory is opened, then the specialties are listed in alphabetical order of their stored name
non_goals: navigation entry or inbound link to the page
notes: New capability distinct from REQ-VET-001 (veterinarian directory): organized by specialty, single page, no paging, separate URL /specialties.html. Open questions resolved by narrowest reading and recorded as assumptions in the PRD: (1) specialties ordered alphabetically by stored name; (2) veterinarians within a specialty in a stable order (alphabetical by last name then first name); (3) a specialty held by no veterinarian still appears with an empty holder list. file_targets are best-effort; system-design-expert may prefer a dedicated SpecialtyController/SpecialtyController tests over extending VetController.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the vet feature package unchanged. Every piece mirrors an existing cataloged sibling, so no new pattern, module, or integration is introduced. Decision: a DEDICATED SpecialtyController + SpecialtyControllerTests, not an extension of VetController. Rationale: the Pattern Catalog 'Web controller' row (system-design.md Contracts) is 'adapts ONE HTTP surface'; the specialty directory is a distinct surface organized around Specialty, so a Specialty-prefixed controller keeps each controller single-responsibility (Design Principle 6) and matches the naming rule 'Controller, prefixed by the domain noun it serves'. Both classes stay in vet/ (Specialty is part of the vet bounded context per ubiquitous-language.md and Package Structure) so no cross-module dependency and no modularity concern. New route GET /specialties.html has no collision with /vets.html or /vets. Specialty ordering is done at the query (ORDER BY name) mirroring PetTypeRepository; veterinarian grouping/ordering within a specialty is a read PROJECTION (not a domain rule), assembled into an immutable value-object view model so it is unit-testable without the web layer.
integration_points: SpecialtyRepository mirrors PetTypeRepository exactly: interface extends JpaRepository<Specialty,Integer>, one @Query("SELECT s FROM Specialty s ORDER BY s.name") List<Specialty> findSpecialties(). Do NOT cache it (PetTypeRepository is uncached; Open Question 5 on vet-cache invalidation stays out of scope).

SpecialtyController is package-private @Controller in vet/, @GetMapping("/specialties.html"), constructor-injected with SpecialtyRepository AND VetRepository (both explicit deps per Design Principle 3). It fetches all specialties (name-ordered) and all vets (VetRepository.findAll()), delegates the grouping to the view-model factory, adds the result to the Model, returns view name "vets/specialtyList".

Grouping: bucket every vet under each Specialty it holds by matching on Specialty identity (id) / name; the full specialty set comes from SpecialtyRepository so a zero-holder specialty still yields an (empty) row. A vet holding no specialty appears in no bucket and is therefore absent. Vets within a bucket sorted by lastName then firstName; render full name as firstName + ' ' + lastName (mirrors vetList.html line 18).

Template vets/specialtyList.html mirrors vetList.html minus the pagination block. Reuse EXISTING message keys only: #{specialties} (heading), #{name} or a specialty/veterinarian column header from existing keys, #{none} for the empty-holder state. All three keys already exist in every one of the 11 messages bundles, so REQ-LANG-002 (no hard-coded text; bundle-key parity build test) stays green with zero new keys.
docs/system-design.md Contracts table updated in this triage: added SpecialtyRepository and SpecialtyController rows wired to REQ-SPEC-001.

patterns.description: Name-ordered lookup-value repository via @Query ORDER BY name — the exact shape SpecialtyRepository copies (grep/Read-confirmed; IDE oracle not connected this run).
Package-private @Controller building a view model and returning a vets/* view — the shape SpecialtyController copies, dropping pagination.

Value object (immutable, equal by value) — the read-projection view-model record fits this In-force pattern; no ADR needed. Name it a domain noun with no prohibited suffix (e.g. SpecialtyListing); the ordering/grouping logic goes in a pure static factory tested mock-free.

risks.risk: A new #{key} added to the template would fail the REQ-LANG-002 bundle-parity build test unless added to all 11 bundles.
risks.mitigation: Reuse the existing specialties/name/none keys; introduce a new key only if unavoidable and then add it to every bundle under src/main/resources/messages/.

risks.risk: Putting the grouping/ordering logic inline in the controller would re-breach the 'no business rule in a web controller' bar and be testable only through MockMvc.
risks.mitigation: Keep the projection in an immutable value-object factory (pure, static); the controller only fetches, delegates, and selects the view. Cover the three ordering/holder ACs with a mock-free unit test on that factory; SpecialtyControllerTests covers routing/model/view.

risks.risk: Testing-policy tension: CLAUDE.md and testing-principles state 'no mocks', but the sibling VetControllerTests uses @WebMvcTest + @MockitoBean. This is a pre-existing codebase-vs-brief contradiction, not introduced by this slice.
risks.mitigation: Not a design blocker. The mock-free path is the value-object factory unit test (the ACs' true home); the controller test may follow the existing @WebMvcTest+@MockitoBean sibling pattern for consistency. Surfaced for the test-reviewer's awareness.

notes: No design-doc-autofix records present since last design-block; autofix audit skipped silently. No ADR warranted: nothing hard-to-reverse or surprising — every type maps to an In-force catalog pattern (Repository, Web controller, Value object). Verdict is minor rather than covered because two new durable contracts were recorded in system-design.md; minor rather than new because no new pattern/module/integration appears. PRD file_targets named VetController/VetRepository as best-effort; this triage overrides to the dedicated-controller + SpecialtyRepository shape per the PRD author's explicit invitation. Next specialist: feature-implementer.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: JPQL @Query is static and parameterless (SELECT s FROM Specialty s ORDER BY s.name) with no user input on the path; showSpecialtyList takes only a Model, so no injection surface exists
All user-derived output (specialty.name, vet full names) rendered via Thymeleaf th:text with default HTML escaping; no th:utext or unescaped sink, so no stored/reflected XSS
No file I/O or dynamic view resolution; view name is the static literal vets/specialtyList, so no path traversal
Read-only @GetMapping flow honors NG-2: no mutating endpoint introduced despite inherited JpaRepository write methods
No dependency or build.gradle changes in this slice; no new supply-chain surface
Data exposed is limited to specialty names and public vet full names; no PII or debug leakage

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Loop variable `vet` iterates over `specialty.veterinarians`, which is a `List<String>` of pre-formatted full names, not `Vet` domain objects. A cold reader encountering `vet` expects a domain type and looks for `vet.firstName`-style property access; the `${vet + " "}` concatenation hints it is a String, but the name still creates a momentary mis-read.
findings.fix: Rename the loop variable to `vetName`: change `th:each="vet : ${specialty.veterinarians}" th:text="${vet + " "}"` to `th:each="vetName : ${specialty.veterinarians}" th:text="${vetName + " "}"`

author: doc-reviewer

findings.description: Rationale prose in PRD: assumption 1 contains the clause 'the narrowest defensible default, as the request left ordering open' which explains WHY alphabetical ordering was chosen. The PRD must describe WHAT the system does; WHY rationale belongs in an ADR referenced via a Design Rationale link. Per prd-authoring prohibited patterns, this is a Critical PRD boundary violation.

The Specialty row's Implements column lists only REQ-VET-001, but Specialty is the central entity of REQ-SPEC-001: SpecialtyRepository fetches Specialty records and SpecialtyController builds the view model from them. The Implements column appears incomplete.

Vet and VetRepository rows list only REQ-VET-001 in Implements. Per the design-block, SpecialtyController injects VetRepository (both explicit deps) and processes Vet objects to fulfill REQ-SPEC-001. Whether REQ-SPEC-001 should be added to these rows' Implements columns requires architectural judgment — the pattern elsewhere (OwnerRepository lists all requirements it serves) suggests yes, but the indirect role of VetRepository here may warrant a different reading.

SpecialtyListing (src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/SpecialtyListing.java) exists in source and encapsulates the core grouping and ordering logic for REQ-SPEC-001 via its static factory, yet has no row in the Contracts table. The table preamble says 'each row names a public type' — SpecialtyListing is package-private — but the design-block identified it as a significant architectural unit. Confirm whether it warrants a Contracts row.

The prd-entry record lists 'Given a veterinarian who holds no specialty, when the directory is opened, then that veterinarian is not shown anywhere on the page' as a formal acceptance criterion (with a matching test name). The PRD places this as edge case 1 rather than a tagged 'Done when' bullet, so it carries no REQ-SPEC-001 tag and is not in the testable-contract section. Confirm whether it should be promoted to a Done when bullet for consistency with the prd-entry contract.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Doc-only resolution of the three doc-reviewer clarify findings (line 13) against docs/system-design.md Contracts. No code, package, or pattern change — the implemented slice already passed all four reviewers. Design unchanged from line 4; this record only completes the Contracts table wiring the earlier triage left incomplete.
notes: Finding 1 (Specialty Implements): ADDED REQ-SPEC-001. Specialty is the central entity of the specialty directory — SpecialtyRepository fetches Specialty records and the view model is built from them — so the row now lists REQ-VET-001, REQ-SPEC-001. Finding 2 (Vet, VetRepository Implements): ADDED REQ-SPEC-001 to both. Judgment: the Implements column records every requirement a type SERVES, not only its aggregate ownership — the OwnerRepository precedent already lists REQ-PET-001 and REQ-VIS-001 it serves indirectly. SpecialtyController constructor-injects VetRepository (explicit dep per Design Principle 3) and processes Vet objects for the grouping, a load-bearing collaboration, not incidental use, so both serve REQ-SPEC-001. Applied consistently: a reader tracing REQ-SPEC-001 now finds every type that serves it, and each type lists every requirement it serves. Preamble strengthened to state the participate-to-serve rule explicitly. Finding 3 (SpecialtyListing row): OMITTED. Judgment: the Contracts convention is public-type-only, and SpecialtyListing is package-private, used solely within vet/ by the controller that owns it; it is the internal read-projection mechanism, not an externally-bound contract. Its grouping/ordering behavior is already carried by the SpecialtyController row purpose prose (grouping veterinarians under each specialty). Adding package-private helpers would bloat the table and set a precedent for cataloging every internal collaborator. Recorded the exclusion rule durably in the Contracts preamble (package-private helpers used only within their owning package are not contracts) so re-review finds the reasoning. Next: doc-reviewer re-review of the changes_requested findings; no implementer work.
